name: Stem & Vow
oneLiner: A wedding florist that takes one order at a time and times every bloom to the hour — everything peaks at the vow.
axisNote: second cinematic-imagery exercise after Ember & Rye — wedding photography IS this vertical's language, so minted fast-prime photography carries the page and the code stays out of the way; the casting doctrine's hardest vertical defused STRUCTURALLY: every human frame is close-crop detail grammar (hands, held bouquets, from-behind) so faces and camera-stares compose out by framing
paletteSeed: the palette IS the countdown: market green-grey (T-72) through bench putty and cool-room dark to van tan and vow gold on cream — ONE deep rose reserved for the handwritten marginalia; refused: blush gauze, shop grids, posed-couple romance, petal-fall
typeDirection: Cormorant Garamond (romantic but EDITORIAL high-contrast serif — never gauze) + Nunito Sans (honest text) + Caveat (the order-book scrawl — the florist's own hand as the soft-organic register) — all OFL, vendored, portfolio-new
motionBudget: one 72-hour countdown told in five chapters with the SAME bouquet as the causal-handoff object in every frame; the scroll grammar is the FOCUS PULL (each chapter photo racks from defocus to sharp at centre-scroll — wedding-film rack focus, the founder's bokeh direction made structural) + a halation veil whose warmth accrues with progress toward T-0; bloom triptych = the lay twin of the timing craft; reduced-motion/no-JS = everything sharp, gentle fixed veil, complete story

verdict.note: 'nothing to change from me actually' — first full-loop site approved no-fix-round; future A+ candidate: scroll-scrubbed bloom-transition video
